title: A prominent protostar in Perseus
caption: The Herbig-Haro object HH 797, imaged by the James Webb Space Telescope
celestial: HH 797 · constellation Perseus · about 1000 light-years away (source figure)
credit: ESA/Webb, NASA & CSA, T. Ray (Dublin Institute for Advanced Studies)

recognition.text: Ranked #88 on ESA/Webb’s published “Top 100 Images” list (an institutional selection, not an audience score).

story: A narrow, brightly colored nebula stretches across the lower half of this view, while above it a glowing point radiates multi-colored light in every direction. This is HH 797, a Herbig-Haro object lying near the young star cluster IC 348, on the eastern side of the Perseus dark cloud complex.

Herbig-Haro objects form when winds or jets from newborn stars smash into nearby gas and dust at high speeds, creating shockwaves that glow. Infrared light escapes the dust around such young stars, so Webb's NIRCam can trace the hot, shocked molecules in the outflows.

Ground-based studies had found a velocity pattern across HH 797 that astronomers once put down to the outflow rotating. Webb's sharper view shows that the single outflow is really two almost parallel ones, each with its own shocks. The source is therefore a pair of stars, each driving its own jet.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (2.42 x 2.34 arcminutes) and distance (1000 light years), the frame spans roughly 0.7 × 0.7 light-years. Its light set out about 1,000 years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This near-infrared image from Webb's NIRCam shows iron and a 1.5-micron filter in purple, molecular hydrogen and methane at about 2 microns in blue, molecular hydrogen at 3.23 microns in cyan, PAH molecules in green, carbon monoxide in orange and molecular hydrogen at 4.7 microns in red.
understand.eye: All of this light is infrared and invisible to the eye, and the young stars' outflows would be hidden by dust in visible light.

explore: The bright infrared objects in the upper part of the image are thought to host two more protostars, and another outflow comes from a protostar top right of center, with its lit cavity walls. HH 797 lies directly north of HH 211, which featured in a Webb release in September 2023.
alt: A narrow, brightly colored horizontal nebula across the lower half, a glowing point radiating multi-colored light above, and a bright star with long spikes at the right edge.
